summary: Eleven comment-endorsed tools, learning resources, apps, and hardware finds from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Minimal Phone
items.summary: An E-paper QWERTY phone whose deliberate friction discourages compulsive scrolling.
items.why_included: An owner said its clunky, text-oriented experience successfully reduced casual phone use.
items.evidence: The owner found the phone unpleasant enough for scrolling but capable enough for essential tasks.

evidence_sources.author: hexapus
evidence_sources.excerpt: The friction of everything being so clunky keeps me from picking it up and staring at it, it's unpleasant to look at and scroll through anything but text.

items.name: Nextcloud
items.source_story_title: Cloud in a Bottle: making self-hosting accessible to everyone
items.summary: A self-hosted file-sync and collaboration platform with desktop and mobile clients.
items.why_included: A three-year user praised its reliability, simple setup, and solid clients.
items.evidence: The commenter reported three trouble-free years and dependable Linux and mobile support.

evidence_sources.author: epihelix
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using it for the last three years (switching over from OwnCloud before that), and it's never missed a beat.

items.name: Nitter
items.source_story_title: Nitter and XCancel resume service after legal advice
items.summary: A privacy-friendly, self-hostable alternative front end for browsing X posts.
items.why_included: A commenter independently praised the project's approachable Nim codebase.
items.evidence: The commenter welcomed Nitter's continuation and found its source surprisingly hackable.

evidence_sources.author: elcritch
evidence_sources.excerpt: Cool to see such a notable Nim based project continue!

items.name: FreeBSD
items.summary: An open-source Unix operating system for desktops, servers, and embedded systems.
items.why_included: An eleven-year daily user praised its broad hardware roles and welcoming community.
items.evidence: The commenter uses FreeBSD across personal computers and servers and strongly endorsed it.

evidence_sources.author: BSDobelix
evidence_sources.excerpt: Overall i really love FreeBSD for everything computing (Pi/Laptop/Workstation/Servers).

items.name: Strudel
items.summary: A browser-based live-coding environment for composing music with compact patterns.
items.why_included: A commenter urged programmers to try it and loved its expressive examples.
items.evidence: The commenter praised Strudel's examples as art made with very little code.

evidence_sources.author: raulparada
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you like those (I love them, so much art in a few lines of code), the docs _will_ get you started. Enjoy!

items.name: Obsidian Web Clipper
items.source_story_title: The ColorChecker, photography's most important 24 squares, turns 50
items.summary: A browser extension that saves readable web content into local Markdown notes.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended its Reading View for escaping ad-heavy article pages.
items.evidence: The commenter advised installing Obsidian Web Clipper and using its Reading View.

evidence_sources.author: DavideNL
evidence_sources.excerpt: Install "Obsidian Web Clipper" and use the "Reading View" button to read articles

items.name: World Graph
items.summary: A geography quiz that represents countries as nodes connected by land borders.
items.why_included: A commenter directly suggested the unusual border-graph guessing game.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended World Graph to readers who enjoyed a topology-themed map.

evidence_sources.author: gus_massa
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you like this, you may like "Guess the countries just from what borders what"

items.name: Designing a Fast, Efficient, Cache-Friendly Hash Table, Step by Step
items.source_story_title: How Swiss tables work in Go built-in map
items.summary: A CppCon talk explaining the engineering path behind Swiss hash tables.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly called it excellent and highly recommended it.
items.evidence: The commenter strongly recommended Matt Kulukundis's talk on Swiss-table development.

evidence_sources.author: nasso_dev
evidence_sources.excerpt: for an excellent talk on the development of swiss tables i highly recommend this talk by Matt Kulukundis at CppCon 2017: "Designing a fast, efficient, cache-friendly hash table, step by step"

items.name: The Jazz Theory Book
items.summary: Mark Levine's practical guide to harmony across jazz and popular music.
items.why_included: A former professional musician strongly recommended its clear, example-rich presentation.
items.evidence: The commenter called the book a great route to understanding jazz and popular harmony.

evidence_sources.author: seanhunter
evidence_sources.excerpt: buy “The Jazz Theory Book” by Mark Levine[1]. In spite of what it says, there really isn’t any such thing as Jazz theory - it’s just music theory, and this book is a great presentation with lots of good examples.

items.name: Notey and Noisy: A Sound Science Mathemusical
items.summary: Mal Webb's 90-minute musical journey through sound, acoustics, and music theory.
items.why_included: A commenter highly recommended setting aside 90 minutes for the listening experience.
items.evidence: The commenter gave Mal Webb's linked sound-science work an unusually emphatic recommendation.

evidence_sources.author: _kb
evidence_sources.excerpt: If this is the sort of thing that interests you, I highly recommend setting aside 90 minutes and strapping yourself in for a listen to

items.name: DIY Color Checker Video
items.source_story_title: The ColorChecker, photography's most important 24 squares, turns 50
items.summary: A video showing how free paint samples can form a useful color target.
items.why_included: A commenter found it useful for building a low-cost photography color checker.
items.evidence: The commenter called the tutorial nice and said it confirms near-match paint colors work well.

evidence_sources.author: mateja
evidence_sources.excerpt: I found this nice video[1] about how to DIY a color checker. He lists the names of the colors in the description. But at least he confirms that even a near match works well!
